description: Perk TOML documents paired with the `[issues] backend`/`team` values the TS subset reader yields (`expected`: extension/substrate/config.ts::resolveIssueDestination via parseTomlSubset — stripped, blank/non-string/absent → null) and whether that read is provably tomllib's (`provable`: resolveIssueRouting reads `keys`; otherwise the save-destination fence widens to the whole `document`). When Python's tomllib reads something else, `tomllib` carries its reading — every such case MUST be unproven. contracts.md §8.23.

cases.name: basic strings
literal strings
multi-line basic strings (unproven: the subset's escape handling is not tomllib's)
multi-line literal strings (unproven: only single-line strings are vouched for)
literal strings keep backslashes verbatim
inline comments after the strings
cases.toml:
[issues]
backend = "linear" # committed
team = 'ENG' # the team key

cases.name: surrounding whitespace is stripped (StrippedStr)
blank strings read as absent (StrippedStr)
other keys in the table and other tables around it
cases.toml:
[workflow]
base = "main"

[issues]
label = "perk"
backend = "github"

[models.stages.plan]
model = "x"

[[ci.checks]]
name = "t"
command = """
just test
"""

cases.name: absent table
absent key
non-string values (unproven: Python's boundary rejects them outright)
empty document
dotted keys (unproven: the subset reader never sees them)
inline table (unproven: the subset reader never sees it)
quoted header (unproven: quoted segments can spell any key)
header with a trailing comment (unproven: the subset reader skips that header)
unicode escape (unproven: the subset reader keeps the escape verbatim)
sub-table (unproven: a super-table the subset reader keeps flat)
array of tables (unproven: tomllib reads a list, never the table)
